description: STAGE 1, written before reading the brief. WHAT IT IS MADE OF: every token is built from three ingredients on a near-black, very slightly blue-grey ground. (1) A large soft sea-green / desaturated teal mass, made of two or three big overlapping ellipses stacked roughly vertically so the silhouette reads as a peanut, capsule or figure-eight; the ellipses are semi-transparent so their overlaps darken into a slightly deeper green core with a paler rim, and a darker teal ghost of the same shape sits behind and offset, like a shadow or a second exposure. (2) A central cluster of pale cream / bone-white translucent quadrilaterals - rotated rectangles and long thin slabs - piled and fanned over the green mass. They multiply and overprint into a brighter, almost white knot at the centre where several overlap. (3) Small squares and diamonds in grey and cream, scattered around the periphery, sometimes in a loose ring, sometimes in a column down one edge, sometimes absent entirely. Everything is flat colour with soft alpha; no line work, no texture, no gradient, no type, no representational imagery. It is not a picture OF anything - the nearest read is a specimen or an X-ray: a soft green body with a bright splintered fracture at its core, or a pale mineral cluster embedded in a green stone. WHAT THE TWELVE SHARE: the palette is identical across all twelve - black ground, one green, one cream, greys. The construction grammar is identical: soft ellipse mass, hard-edged pale slabs, scatter squares. The centre of gravity is the middle of the frame in every one. WHAT DIFFERS ACROSS THE TWELVE SEEDS: mainly how much of each ingredient there is and how far it spreads. 9011, 9369 and 10801 are the quiet ones - a big green peanut with a small tight cream knot near the middle and almost nothing else; these three are close enough to each other to be confusable. 9548 and 10264 are the same recipe with the cream knot exploded into a wide radiating burst that reaches the green edge. 9190, 10443 and 10980 replace the compact knot with long thin bars crossing at wide angles, an asterisk or pick-up-sticks read. 9727 adds a hard vertical column of grey and cream squares down the left edge and a matching file of diamonds on the right, the only token with that framing device. 9906, 10085 and 10622 are the outliers: in these the green mass has all but vanished - 10085 has none visible at all, 9906 has a bare smear behind the bars, 10622 has one green ellipse fragment at the lower left - and the frame is instead filled with grey and cream slabs on black. 10622 is the strongest outlier by a distance: large opaque grey and cream rectangles stacked in near-horizontal courses, running off all four edges, reading as a completely different work from a completely different collection. WHAT HAPPENS ACROSS THE THREE STATES: I have four seeds by three states (9011, 9190, 9369, 9548 in neutral, stress, recovery). The colour does not change at all - same green, same cream, same black in all three rows. What changes is scale, spread and arrangement. Going neutral to stress the green mass generally grows and rounds out, its two lobes separating into more distinctly readable circles, and the pale cluster shifts position and loosens - in 9369 stress the two pale rectangles that sat at the left and right edges swell into big flat slabs and the cream knot slides up and left, which is the clearest single state change on the sheet. Going to recovery the cream cluster tends to grow denser and fan wider - 9548 recovery has visibly more slabs reaching further out than 9548 neutral, and 9011 recovery fans downward-left where neutral was tighter. 9190 stress leans its bars more horizontal and thickens them; 9190 recovery re-radiates them. So the transition is a redistribution and a slight inflation, not a change of kind: nothing breaks, nothing fractures, nothing darkens, nothing new appears, and no state has a mood the others lack. If I had to name it I would say the object breathes slightly rather than reacts. WHAT SURVIVES AT 120px: the green peanut survives completely - it is the only thing that reads instantly, and it is what tells one token from another at browse size. The cream cluster survives as a bright smudge and you can tell a compact knot (9011, 9369, 10801) from a wide burst (9548, 10264) from crossed sticks (9190, 10443), but the individual slabs, their rotations and their overprinting all dissolve. The scatter squares survive only as specks and 9727s square column survives as a recognisable device. The three states at 120 are close: 9369 stress is distinguishable from 9369 neutral by the swollen side slabs, 9548 recovery is denser than 9548 neutral, but 9011 across all three states and 9190 across all three states read as the same picture nudged, and if the rows were unlabelled and shuffled I do not think I could sort them reliably. ARTIFACTS I NOTICE: in 10622 the slabs are cut hard by all four frame edges and the composition reads as a crop of something larger rather than a composed frame. In 9727 the left-hand squares are clipped by the left edge. In 9369 and 9011 the pale rectangles at the left and right sit half on and half off the green mass and read as accidental collisions rather than placed elements. In 9906 and 10085 the near-total absence of the green mass makes the token look like a render that failed to draw its background layer rather than a deliberate variant.
